:JUDGMENT:
This is a Petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- for the death of Sandeep S/o Vishwanath in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. Brief averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 17.10.2022 at about 6.45 a.m., on Malur-Kolar Road near Ajantha Weighbridge, Malur Town, while Sandeep (deceased) was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing no.KA-53-HJ-1531 with his friend - Bharath as pillion, a Maruthi EECO Car bearing no.
KA-08-M-7812 driven by its driver at high-speed in a rash and negligent manner,
came from opposite-direction and dashed against the Honda Activa.

As a result,
Sandeep & Bharath fell-down and sustained grievous-injuries.

Sandeep was Vishwanath vs S.M. Narayanaswamy on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188068117/
2 immediately shifted to Government Hospital where he was declared 'brought dead'.
3.

sentences.text: That prior to accident, Sandeep was hale and healthy.
He was working as a Civil Engineer and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
4. That the sole cause of the accident was the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
Hence Respondent no.1 being the owner and Respondent no.2 being the insurer of the car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Thus it is prayed to allow the petition.
5. Respondent no.1 & 2 have appeared through their counsel.
However, only respondent no.3 has filed the Objections Statement.
Originally, Respondent no.2 was shown as the 'Insurer' of the offending car.

But later, on the ground that the 'third-party' insurance of the offending car was covered by Respondent no.3-Insurance Company, Respondent no.3 was impleaded in the suit, and Respondent no.2 was 'deleted' from the cause-title of the petition.
6. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.3-Insurance Company has denied the petition-averments.
It is contended that the accident was due to the negligence of the rider of the deceased himself who was riding the scooter without wearing the helmet.
That the rider of the Motor-cycle was not holding a valid, effective driving license.
Thus, it is prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

7. On the rival pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal-representatives of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Mr.Sandeep died due to injuries sustained by him in an Accident occurred on 17-10-2022 at about 6.45 p.m. near Ajantha weigh bridge, Malur-Kolar road, Malur taluk, arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of EECO car bearing Reg. No.KA-08-M- 7812?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
8. On behalf of petitioners, petitioner no.1 has been examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P.1 to 19 have been marked ; an eye-witness has been examined as PW.2.
On the other hand, Respondent no.3 has not adduced any evidence.

10. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2: This issue is taken-up first since it has a bearing on other issues.

As per the petition, one Sandeep who is the son of petitioner no.1, 2 and brother of petitioner no.2 has died in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the driver of the offending car bearing no.KA-08- M-7812.

On the other hand, Respondent no.3-Insurance Company has denied that the accident was due to the rash & negligent driving by the driver of the car bearing no.KA-08-M-7812.
12.
In support of the case of Petitioners, Petitioner no.1 has been examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P.1 to 19 have been marked.

Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.9 are the Police Documents viz., certified-copy of FIR,
Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Notice under Section 133 of MV Act & its Reply, IMV Report, Inquest,
P.M. Report and Charge sheet.

13. The FIR & Complaint at Exs.P.1 & 2 show that the case has been registered against the driver of the offending car bearing no.KA-08-M-7812 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337,
304A of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar which gives a description of the accident spot.
Ex.P.4 is the Notice under Section 133 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.5 is Reply to said Notice given by the Owner of the car.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report which shows that the front-portion of the Honda Activa Scooter has been fully-damaged whereas the front right-side of the car has been damaged.
This corroborates the fact that the car coming from the opposite-direction has dashed against the Activa Scooter.
However, the Spot Sketch has not been placed on record, which would have otherwise shown the exact accident spot.
Ex.P.7 is the Inquest.
Ex.P.8 is the P.M. Report which shows the cause of death was 'haemarrhagic shock resulted due to head injury with polytrauma'.
Ex.P.8 thus corroborates the injuries sustained and the consequent death of deceased Sandeep.
Ex.P.9 is the Charge sheet filed against the driver of the car for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337, 304A of IPC.
Exs.P.11 to 14 are notarized-copy of Aadhar card of petitioners and deceased.
Ex.P.15 is copy of SSLC marks card of deceased.
Ex.P.16 is Study certificate, Ex.P.17 is Diploma certificate and Ex.P.18 and 19 are Marks card of 2nd Semester and 6th Semester.

sentences.text: Ex.P.9 is the charge sheet which discloses that after thorough investigation, the I.O has filed the charge-sheet against S.M.Narayanaswamy - the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337, 304A of IPC.
On the contrary, respondent no.3 has although denied the negligence of the driver of the offending car, has not examined its driver to prove its contention.
But after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed the Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending car and the same has not been challenged by its driver.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the rashness &
negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car, has led to the death of Sandeep.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the "Affirmative".
15.
Issue No.1 and 3
: Since these issues are interlinked, they are taken-up together for discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
As per the petition, petitioner no.1 is father, petitioner no.2 is the mother and petitioner no.3 is the sister of deceased Sandeep.
In support of this fact, the Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioner no.1 to 3 at Exs.P.10 to 14 have been produced.
The relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased is thus proved.
Moreover, there is no dispute about the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
Thus petitioner no.1 to 3 are the legal-representatives of deceased Sandeep.
16. As per the petition, the deceased was aged about 24 years as on the date of accident.
The Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.10 which shows his date of birth as 18.02.1998 corroborates this fact.
The age of deceased Sandeep is thus 24 years as on the date of accident.
17. Next, as per the petition, the deceased was working as a Civil Engineer and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Petitioners have not produced any document to prove the occupation and income of deceased.

However, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.15 - SSLC Marks card of deceased, Ex.P.16 - Study certificate, Ex.P.17 is Diploma Certificate and Ex.P.18 and 19 are Marks cards of Diploma 2nd & 6th Semester.

In support of his argument that the educational qualification of the deceased who is a Diploma Holder is to be considered while assessing his income, the learned counsel for petitioner has relied-on the decisions reported in:
1. 2020 Supreme (KAR) 1335 Relevant para-7 between Sherly Jeevan Vs.R.K.S.Infra Tech Pvt.Ltd.,
2. 2024 ACJ 658 Relevant para-8 between Kumud Gupta and another Vs. Iffco-Tokio General Ins.Co.Ltd., & others.
Unlike in the present petition where the deceased is a Diploma Holder

sentences.text: , the deceased in both these cases were the students of Degree in Engineering; and considering the fact that they had good future prospects, the 'income' of the deceased has been analysed in these cases.

Whereas in the case on hand, considering the fact that the deceased was a Diploma Holder and a 'fresher' out of college,
aged only about 24 years as on the date of accident, it is proper to take the notional income of the Vishwanath vs S.M. Narayanaswamy on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188068117/
5 deceased as Rs.15,500/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, since the said accident has been occurred in the year 2022.

sentences.text: With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.
18. As discussed above, the deceased has left behind his father, mother and sister as dependents.

As per the decision reported in AIR 2017 S.C. 5157 - National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others: The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rs.15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rs.40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-.

entities.text: AIR 2017 S.C. 5157 - National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said amount has to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years".
Petitioner no.1 & 2 who are the parents of deceased have lost the love & affection of their son.

Therefore, petitioner no.1 & 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.88,000/- (Rs.44,000/- x 2) under the Head of Loss of Consortium;
Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards Loss of Estate and Rs.16,500/- towards Funeral Expenses.
19. Next, it is pertinent to note that as per the detailed discussion made supra, the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m.

In the decision reported in AIR 2017 S.C. 5157 - National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others: The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case of persons who is below 40 years and are self- employed or have fixed salary, there should be an addition of 40% to the income, towards future prospects".

entities.text: AIR 2017 S.C. 5157 - National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was of 24 years on the date of accident.
Hence towards future prospects, 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,500/- comes to Rs.6,200/-.
Therefore, the income of deceased comes to Rs.21,700/- p.m. (Rs.15,500 + Rs.6,200).
20. As per the principle laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 - Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another: the multiplier applicable is '18'.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 - Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Admittedly,
deceased Sandeep was a 'Bachelor'.
In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is bachelor", 50% of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
In the case on hand, the deceased was a 'bachelor', and petitioner no.1 to 3 are his dependents.
Hence 50% of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

On deducting 50% of the amount towards his personal-expenses out of his income of Rs.21,700/-, it comes to Rs.10,850/- p.m (21,700 - 10,850) and on applying the multiplier '18', it comes to Rs.23,43,600/- (Rs.10,850 x 12 x 18 = Rs.23,43,600/-) .
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,43,600/- towards loss of dependency.

21. Considering the above aspects, petitioners are entitled for total compensation as under :
1. Loss of Dependency Rs.23,43,600/-
2. Loss of Consortium Rs. 88,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5.

Total Rs.24,64,600/-

6
Thus, the Petitioners are awarded the total compensation of Rs.24,65,000/- (rounded-off) with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
22. Regarding Liability
: As already discussed above, the petitioners have proved that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car bearing no. KA-52-A-2609.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of Insurance Policy of the offending-vehicle.
Therefore, Respondent no.1 being the Owner & Respondent no.3 being the Insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, Respondent no.3 being the Insurer has to indemnify the Insured/Owner, and it has to deposit the compensation amount with interest.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative & Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.4 : In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
A sum of Rs.24,65,000/- is awarded as total compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.
Respondent no.1 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Respondent no.3 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Petitioner no.1 is entitled to 40% of the total compensation awarded.

Out of which 50% of the award amount is ordered to be released to Petitioner no.1 by way of E-Payment after proper identification, and the remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner no.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
Petitioner no.2 is entitled to 40% of the total compensation awarded.

Out of which 50% of the award amount is ordered to be released to Petitioner no.1 by way of E-Payment after proper identification, and the remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner no.2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
Petitioner no.4 is entitled to 20% of the total compensation awarded.

Out of which 50% of the award amount is ordered to be released to Petitioner no.1 by way of E-Payment after proper identification, and the remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner no.4 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1,000/-.
